name: Vorrenth Major
geological_features: Layered metallic hydrogen ocean beneath the cloud deck
Persistent cyclonic storm systems spanning thousands of kilometers
Ammonia ice crystal bands in the upper atmosphere
Radiation belts generated by a powerful magnetic field
specific_features: A hexagonal polar vortex visible in infrared wavelengths
A faint ring system composed of captured asteroid debris
Aurorae of extraordinary intensity at both magnetic poles
description: Vorrenth Major dominates its orbital neighborhood with a mass sufficient to shepherd asteroid belts and perturb the orbits of neighboring worlds. Its cloud bands ripple in alternating stripes of pale amber and deep ochre, driven by jet streams exceeding two thousand kilometers per hour at the equatorial zone.

The atmosphere deepens from wispy ammonia clouds into increasingly dense layers of hydrogen and helium, eventually transitioning into a vast ocean of metallic hydrogen under crushing pressure. Electromagnetic discharges arc between cloud layers in silent, sprawling displays that dwarf any terrestrial lightning by orders of magnitude.

Vorrenth Major's powerful magnetosphere creates some of the most intense radiation belts observed in the region, making close approach hazardous for unshielded vessels. A faint ring system, likely captured from a destroyed moon or passing asteroid, orbits at a shallow angle, its particles slowly spiraling inward over geological timescales.

The gas giant's primary value lies in its atmosphere, which contains substantial reserves of helium-3 and other fusion fuels harvestable by atmospheric skimmer operations. Its system of seventeen moons offers potential staging points, though the radiation environment demands significant shielding for any prolonged presence in the Vorrenth system.
